elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Retained § 11.4 triggers "Commencing six (6) months prior to the expiration of the Term of this Agreement, or upon any termination of this Agreement for any reason," and the inserted paragraph applies "Within thirty (30) days after the expiration or termination of this Agreement" — both exit routes are covered.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: § 11.4: "M&I shall continue to provide Customer all Services at the rates set forth in this Agreement, for a maximum period of six (6) months," plus an unlimited-duration duty to provide "all necessary assistance" from six months before expiry or upon any termination. The 100-day written-request condition is a mechanic, not an undefined trigger, and is correctly noted rather than redlined.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: § 11.4: "all Expenses and charges for Termination Assistance shall be computed in accordance with M&I's then-current rates for such products, materials and services."

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Within thirty (30) days after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, M&I shall return all Customer Data to Customer" — unconditional, anchored to expiry/termination (not to a request), and covering "all Customer Data" as defined in § 17.1.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Inserted: return "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" — equivalent to the standard machine-readable format required by the element.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Inserted: M&I "shall, following completion of any Termination Assistance, delete all Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing." Deletion is deferred (not immediate) and written certification is express; the unconditional 30-day return duty controls, so certified deletion follows the return in operation.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language in retained § 11.4 ("expiration of the Term ... or upon any termination ... for any reason") and in the inserted data-return paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: § 11.4 permits continued Services "for a maximum period of six (6) months," which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph requires return of all Customer Data in machine-readable form within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination.

reasons: Deviation call is correct: as originally drafted the agreement had transition assistance (§ 11.4) but no data-return or export mechanic at all — § 17.1 only allocates ownership and § 17.5 only imposes security safeguards — which fails even the fallback (export within 30 days) and sits in walk-away territory ("no data return").

The redline reaches the preferred level: trigger, six-month duration and then-current-rate elements are already met by retained § 11.4, and the single inserted paragraph supplies the three missing elements (30-day return, machine-readable format, certified deletion).

Minimality holds: one concise insertion for a missing mechanic, no deletions or paraphrase of existing text, no survival tail, no added expense/damages/procedural boilerplate, and Customer-favourable retained language (contract-rate continuation, the right to decline Termination Assistance) is preserved.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is expressly anchored to "following completion of any Termination Assistance," so it does not cut short the retained six-month assistance mechanic, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Optional tightening (not a failure): anchor deletion to "following such return and completion of any Termination Assistance" so that, where Customer declines Termination Assistance under the last sentence of § 11.4, the deletion trigger cannot arguably arise before the 30-day return is performed. Also give the new paragraph a section number (e.g. § 11.5) to match the comment.
